title: Pixel Pet (bug hunt)
body:
Goal: use your debugging strategies to fix three bugs in a virtual pet program.

The rules:

  • feed(): hunger goes down by 3 (never below 0).
  • play(): happiness goes up by 2 and hunger goes up by 1.
  • mood(): the pet is "grumpy" if hunger is 8 or more or happiness is 2 or less. Otherwise it is "happy".
  1. Open starter.py and press Run. Read the traceback bottom-up: bug 1.
  2. After bug 1 is fixed, look at the printed dictionary. Does it have a key it should not have? That is bug 2.
  3. Bug 3 does not crash. Read mood() out loud and compare it with the rules.

Done looks like:

{'name': 'Pixel', 'hunger': 4, 'happiness': 9}
Pixel feels happy.

Write a bug report for each bug on your homework sheet.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the red text from the bottom up to find bug 1. Then compare the rules in the README with each function: feed(), play() and mood(). Look closely at every word inside the quote marks.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Dictionary keys must match exactly, including capital letters and spelling. A key that is not there causes a KeyError, and a misspelled key you assign to makes a new one. For mood(), read the rule again and look at the joining word.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Run the program and compare the keys in the printed dictionary with the ones in make_pet(). Fix each key so it matches exactly. For bug 3, read the rule out loud, then check the word between the two conditions in mood(). Does it say the same thing?

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Homework Bug Hunt: Pixel Pet
# A virtual pet stored in a dictionary. There are THREE bugs.
# Press Run and read the traceback bottom-up to find the first one.


def make_pet(name):
    """Return a new pet. Hunger and happiness go from 0 to 10."""
    return {"name": name, "hunger": 5, "happiness": 5}


def feed(pet):
    """Feeding makes the pet less hungry (but never below 0)."""
    pet["Hunger"] = pet["hunger"] - 3
    if pet["hunger"] < 0:
        pet["hunger"] = 0
    return pet


def play(pet):
    """Playing makes the pet happier and a little hungrier."""
    pet["happiness"] = pet["happiness"] + 2
    pet["hunger"] = pet["hungry"] + 1
    return pet


def mood(pet):
    """Return "grumpy" if the pet is very hungry OR very unhappy, else "happy"."""
    if pet["hunger"] >= 8 and pet["happiness"] <= 2:
        return "grumpy"
    return "happy"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pet = make_pet("Pixel")
    play(pet)
    play(pet)
    feed(pet)
    print(pet)
    print(f"{pet['name']} feels {mood(pet)}.")
